slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will unrot
your brain

building model kits

build a model plane, ship or city with your hands, one small piece at a time. slow, detailed work rebuilds the patience that endless short videos wore away.

reading paper newspapers

buy a paper newspaper on sunday and read it slowly with breakfast. a finite set of stories, read properly and slowly, is the exact opposite of an endless feed.

one real lesson a day

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson about something real: how volcanoes work, a famous artist, an ancient empire. real knowledge is the best cure for brain rot.
slides.texte_sophia:
one real lesson a day

i spend 5 minutes a day on one real lesson: how volcanoes work, a famous artist. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and real knowledge is the best cure for brain rot.

slides.texte_overlay:
learning chess

play one slow game of chess a day, online or in person. thinking several moves ahead trains the deep, patient attention that short clips quietly destroy.

writing letters

write one handwritten letter a week to someone you love. choosing words slowly and carefully brings back a kind of focus most of us have forgotten we had.
